issues.description: Inconsistent getter naming for the StockIngredient.name field between template and solution. The template's StockIngredient exposes getIngredientName(), and the template's Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getIngredientName(). The solution, however, uses getName() in StockIngredient and calls getName() in Stock.findStockIngredient(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not mandate a specific method name; this cross-repository difference in method names can confuse students comparing template and reference solution or when tests/reference expect a specific getter name.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single, consistent getter name for the StockIngredient.name field across template, tests, and reference solution (either getName() or getIngredientName()). Update the template StockIngredient and Stock.findStockIngredient to use that chosen name, and update the reference solution (or vice versa) so both repositories match. Also clarify in the problem statement that getters should follow the chosen naming convention to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient name is named inconsistently across artifacts. The template repository defines getIngredientName() (used by template Stock.findStockIngredient), while the solution repository uses getName() (and solution Stock.findStockIngredient calls getName()). The problem statement refers to a name field but does not specify a getter name. This mismatch (getIngredientName vs getName) refers to the exact same conceptual entity (the ingredient's name) and can confuse students when mapping the template code to the provided solution or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the getter name across template and solution. For example, rename getIngredientName() in the template to getName(), and update any calls (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to use getName(). Alternatively, change the solution to use getIngredientName(). Prefer using getName() for brevity and update all references accordingly.
